text: Welcome to the capstone. Over the next several lessons you'll build one complete data governance program for a single fictional company — LTV Global — applying everything you've learned across this entire career path.

LTV Global is a fictional, illustrative mid-sized multinational consumer-products company — outdoor and home goods, roughly forty-eight hundred employees, headquartered in Atlanta with offices in Leeds and Singapore. It is not a real business; it exists purely so this capstone has one consistent scenario to build against.

Its data lives in five fictional systems: Atlas, the ERP system of record for orders and products; Beacon, the sales CRM; Comet, the e-commerce storefront; Harbor, the warehouse system; and Summit, the governed analytics layer almost nothing feeds reliably today.

A UK customer's data access request took six weeks and four departments to answer, and two systems returned different order histories for the same person. That gap reached the board, and new Chief Data Officer Dana Whitfield was given a mandate to build a real governance program, starting now.

Over the next eleven lessons you'll build one continuous deliverable set: a data landscape inventory, scored critical data elements, named owners and stewards, a glossary and dictionary, sensitivity classification, real SQL quality checks, a lineage trace, authoritative sources, access and retention policies, governance KPIs, and finally an operating model.
Next: Lesson 2 reviews LTV Global's full data landscape — mapping every system before you can govern any of them.
